facts.raw_span: Gradual hair loss of the eyelashes, eyebrows, beard, and scalp for 4 years
Swelling and painful hand joints for 13 months
Multiple asymptomatic nodules on the upper arms for 40 days
No fever
No previous infections, family history, or personal medical history of autoimmune diseases or psoriasis
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate: 27 mm/h (slightly elevated)
Rheumatoid factor: 70.1 IU/mL (significantly elevated)
Normal results for: C-reactive protein, anticyclic citrullinated peptide, antinuclear antibodies, and globulin levels
X-ray and joint ultrasound showed: osteoarthritis, synovitis, flexor tendon tenosynovitis, and bone erosions
Diffuse infiltrate of foamy histiocytes in the dermis (hematoxylin-eosin stain)
Numerous acid-fast bacilli present (acid-fast stain)
Fundus fluorescein angiography showed uveitis

concepts.why: The combination of hair loss, joint symptoms, skin nodules, and elevated rheumatoid factor, along with the presence of acid-fast bacilli and granulomatous inflammation on skin biopsy, are consistent with sarcoidosis.

The presence of skin nodules and granulomatous inflammation on skin biopsy, along with the combination of hair loss and joint symptoms, are consistent with lupus pernio, a form of cutaneous sarcoidosis.

The combination of joint symptoms, elevated rheumatoid factor, and synovitis on joint ultrasound are consistent with rheumatoid arthritis, although the presence of skin nodules and granulomatous inflammation on skin biopsy are not typical of this condition.
The presence of acid-fast bacilli on skin biopsy is consistent with tuberculosis, although the clinical presentation and other laboratory findings are not typical of this condition.

The combination of hair loss, joint symptoms, skin nodules, and granulomatous inflammation on skin biopsy are consistent with granulomatosis with polyangiitis, although the presence of acid-fast bacilli and the clinical presentation are not typical of this condition.

The presence of skin nodules and granulomatous inflammation on skin biopsy are consistent with erythema nodosum, although the combination of hair loss and joint symptoms are not typical of this condition.
The presence of uveitis on fundus fluorescein angiography is consistent with this condition, although it is often associated with other systemic diseases such as sarcoidosis or rheumatoid arthritis.
The presence of osteoarthritis on joint ultrasound is consistent with this condition, although it is often associated with other systemic diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis or sarcoidosis.
The presence of synovitis on joint ultrasound is consistent with this condition, although it is often associated with other systemic diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis or sarcoidosis.

The presence of flexor tendon tenosynovitis on joint ultrasound is consistent with this condition, although it is often associated with other systemic diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis or sarcoidosis.
